title: Inequalities
summary: Express comparisons using less than, greater than, less than or equal to, and greater than or equal to.
objectives: Choose the correct inequality symbol for a comparison.
Describe all integers satisfying a compound inequality.

sections.title: Read an inequality as a complete statement

blocks.text: The symbols < and > describe strict comparisons, while ≤ and ≥ include equality. Read from left to right:
means a is less than b, and
means a is greater than or equal to b. The wider side of < or > faces the greater value. A reliable check is to say the statement aloud rather than relying only on the symbol's shape.

sections.title: A compound inequality describes an interval

blocks.text: combines two conditions: x is greater than -2 and x is at most 3. On a number line, use an open point when the endpoint is excluded (< or >) and a filled point when it is included (≤ or ≥). Both conditions must be satisfied at the same time.
When the variable is restricted to integers, locate the two endpoints, decide whether each endpoint is included, and list the whole-number steps between them. Do not include fractional values. For
. Checking the first and last listed values against both inequality signs prevents endpoint mistakes.

sections.title: Worked example: translate a real condition

prompt.text: A storage temperature must be above
. Write an inequality for the temperature

content.text: “Above -4” excludes -4, so use a strict inequality.
“No higher than 3” includes 3, so use less than or equal to.
Combine the two limits in increasing order.

sections.verification_note: A value such as 0 satisfies both limits, -4 is excluded, and 3 is included.

sections.title: Worked example: list values in an interval

content.text: The filled lower endpoint includes -2. The open upper endpoint excludes 4.
Move through the integer steps between the endpoints.

sections.verification_note: The first value equals the included lower bound, and the last integer is the greatest value still below 4.

feedback.text: The integers are -2, -1, 0, 1 and 2. The lower endpoint -3 is excluded and the upper endpoint 2 is included.

blocks.text: Translate each comparison word carefully, distinguish strict from inclusive endpoints, write compound inequalities in increasing order, use open or filled endpoints consistently, and test boundary values before finalising an interval or list of integers.
